tips.text: All-in when he extends toward your tower. His kill pressure dies past the midpoint while yours starts, so let him overreach first.
tips.heading: Extended punish

tips.text: Throw E only when his movement locks inside a Q cast. A free E is the trigger he plays around, while a forced one starts your all-in.
tips.heading: Committed E

guides.favoredWhen: Dodge E with E, deny his W heals with Ignite, and all-in after his stolen R lands.

keyTips.text: Level 1, stand behind minions against his E: the opener is positional.
Dodge his E with your E, then E2 plus passive plus shroud: the full answer.
Ignite before heals and deny his W heals: no healing means no comeback.

tips.text: Dodge Q2: the second blast is the damage.
His E2 interrupts your dashes: E once, commit after.
His stolen R comes back later than yours: all-in after he spends it.
Shroud the extended trade: your stealth outlasts his cooldowns.
Heals denied plus stolen-R punished: the Sylas who never sustains never wins.

guides.favoredWhen: Your dashes feed her passive. Engage only after she wastes it on the wave.

keyTips.text: Your dashes refill her passive: every E feeds her fear.
Dodge spells, especially fear on red passive: marked means death.
When stacked, her W cancels dashes: never E into a stacked Vex.

tips.text: Poke without dashing: Qs do not feed the mark.
Concede dash trades early: feet first, blades later.
Engage only after she wastes passive on waves: empty marks are safe marks.
Track the red glow: passive-up means hands-off.
Passive starved plus dashes safe: the Vex who never fears you never wins.

guides.favoredWhen: Very easy unless he snowballs. Q when he farms, dodge Q, and answer Q3 with E.

keyTips.text: Very easy lane: press every edge from level 1.
Q when he farms: his last-hit is your poke.
Dodge his Q: sidesteps deny his whole pattern.

tips.text: His Q3 onto you gives a free E: the knockup is your engage.
Starve the sustain snowball: no early kills means no threat.
His W shield has a delay: Q then shroud to beat it.
Keep poking between shields: delay windows are damage windows.
Never-fed Yone: the snowball denied is the game won.

sources.rankClaim: Master (profile badge; title claims 2000LP GrandMaster EUW and Challenger EUNE) · Akali main

guides.favoredWhen: Akali controls short trades and denies grit; Sett only wins extended fights with Facebreaker and Haymaker available.

keyTips.text: Never take auto-auto-Q trades early. Hit Q plus a passive auto, then leave before his Q move speed lets him turn the extended fight and stack grit.
keyTips.heading: Trading rule

keyTips.text: Bait Facebreaker at max range and shroud the moment he steps in for it. Without E he cannot flip you, and his whole extended-trade plan falls apart.
keyTips.heading: Beating Facebreaker

keyTips.text: Hold E or R for Haymaker and only commit when his W or E is gone. If he burns either on the wave, that missing cooldown is your all-in window.
keyTips.heading: Haymaker discipline

tips.text: Levels 1 to 3, poke with Q and proc the passive auto, then step out immediately. A second auto lets him stick with Q move speed and build the grit you are trying to deny.
tips.heading: Levels 1–3

tips.text: Expect Grasp and W max with defensive itemization. He wants repeated bruising trades, so give him single Q procs instead and keep E or R ready because Haymaker cycles back fast.
tips.heading: His setup

tips.text: Kite every extended fight with passive move speed, Q and E. The moment Facebreaker is available again, break contact at max range or shroud it rather than standing in flip range.
tips.heading: Kiting pattern

tips.text: Watch his cooldown use on the wave. When Haymaker or Facebreaker hits minions, engage at once since he has no answer left for your full rotation.
tips.heading: Punish wave use

tips.text: Take fights only with shroud plus E or R ready. With that combination up you dictate the trade, and without it you give ground, because a straight stat-check into his cooldowns is the one way he turns the lane.
tips.heading: Fight selection

If your E lands, hold E2 to track her through invis and R dashes.
Your engages are straight lines: her linears hit you on the way in, so angle them.

tips.text: Survive the early: shield start concedes nothing later.
Land E before committing: no mark means no follow.
Track through every dash: held E2 is your only stick.
Engage off-angles only: straight lines die.
Survived plus stuck: the Aurora who never shook you never wins.

keyTips.text: Accept a weaker lane before level 6, with the most early pressure available into melee opponents.
Treat level 6 plus the first finished item as the moment to fight for objectives and kills.
Value mid game highly, since carries often still lack magic resistance at that stage.

tips.text: Start Doran's Shield into poke or burst lanes to survive the early stretch.
Start Doran's Ring with two potions into melee lanes without poke for a more aggressive edge.
Take Flash and Ignite as the standard summoner pair.
Pick Electrocute into squishy teams for burst, or Conqueror for longer trades into bruisers and tanks.
Use the level-6 and first-item windows to contest objectives and hunt kills.
Turn one successful roam or teamfight into recovery from a bad lane, since a kill can start a gold and damage snowball.
Spend mobility and shroud on escaping ganks and repositioning inside fights.
Reach squishy targets with burst around the level-6 and first-item spikes, using the ultimate execute.
Aim for the backline in teamfights, but wait out dangerous crowd control and engage cooldowns before committing.
Refuse tanky, magic-resistance-heavy teams as burst targets, since her damage falls off sharply into them.

itemization.text: Take Conqueror for extended fights and bruiser or tank crowds, with Presence of Mind for energy, Legend: Tenacity, and Coup de Grace.
Take Electrocute for squishy teams or when allies handle tanks, with Sudden Impact, Grisly Mementos, and Ultimate Hunter.
Pick Resolve by matchup: Second Wind into poke, Bone Plating into close-range burst, Unflinching when crowd control matters, Overgrowth for extra health otherwise.
Build Hextech Gunblade into Sorcerer's Shoes, Shadowflame, Zhonya's Hourglass, Rabadon's Deathcap, and Void Staff.

keyTips.text: Farm safely and protect health until W, E, and R are all online.
At level 6, threaten an all-in with R when the opponent overextends.
Prefer picks and split fights over a straight 5v5, where grouped enemies and defensive items deny clean kills.

tips.text: Use Q to hit the wave while keeping the opponent under threat at the same time.
Check energy before any all-in and track the enemy jungler, since Akali invites early camps before level 6.
Treat E as both engage and escape, and never waste it when it may be needed to leave.
After the first component and a recall, trade more often since Q hits harder.
At level 3, use the full basic kit for trades without chasing so far that the exchange turns.
Shove with Q, then roam toward an extended lane, using E and R to close the gap.
At neutral objectives, show E so enemy carries respect the follow-up and give ground instead of forcing a dive.
Save W for a real fight opening; spending it early lets opponents bait a bad all-in.
Pick the longer side lane when safe, since extra space helps commit to an isolated target.
At level 9, use maxed Q for faster clearing and stronger side-lane duels.
At level 11, use the second R rank to catch isolated enemies more often.
Turn a mid-game pick into a numbers edge for a Baron call.
Snowball isolated squishy kills into further picks with the earned lead.
Before committing late, account for nearby backup, since grouped opponents ruin clean assassinations.
Stay patient in teamfights and keep W for the entry or the escape window.
At level 16, use the third R rank and its lower cooldown for more late-fight windows.

itemization.text: Trade more aggressively after the first component, since it directly raises Q damage.
Scout Zhonya's Hourglass and Guardian Angel on late opponents and hold the commit until their answers are mapped.
